original_value: AbstractThis research proposes an improved hybrid fusion scheme for non‐subsampled contourlet transform (NSCT) and stationary wavelet transform (SWT). Initially, the source images are decomposed into different sub‐bands using NSCT. The locally weighted sum of square of the coefficients based fusion rule with consistency verification is used to fuse the detailed coefficients of NSCT. The SWT is employed to decompose approximation coefficients of NSCT into different sub‐bands. The entropy of square of the coefficients and weighted sum‐modified Laplacian is employed as the fusion rules with SWT. The final output is obtained using inverse NSCT. The proposed research is compared with existing fusion schemes visually and quantitatively. From the visual analysis, it is observed that the proposed scheme retained important complementary information of source images in a better way. From the quantitative comparison, it is seen that this scheme gave improved edge information, clarity, contrast, texture, and brightness in the fused image.

result.paraphrase: This study presents an enhanced hybrid fusion method combining the non-subsampled contourlet transform (NSCT) and stationary wavelet transform (SWT). The source images are first decomposed into multiple sub-bands with NSCT, and the NSCT detail coefficients are fused using a locally weighted sum-of-squares rule with consistency verification. Next, SWT is applied to decompose the NSCT approximation coefficients into additional sub-bands, which are then fused using the square-of-coefficients entropy and weighted sum-modified Laplacian rules. The final image is reconstructed through inverse NSCT. The proposed method is evaluated against existing fusion schemes both visually and quantitatively. Visual results show that it preserves important complementary information from the source images more effectively, while quantitative comparison indicates better edge information, clarity, contrast, texture, and brightness in the fused image.
